$comment: P62 lane ae — [[D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-ARG-CONSTANT-EXPRESSION]], the RUNNABLE half. An attribute argument is a CONSTANT-EXPRESSION: the keyword-led primaries (`sizeof`, `_Alignof`, `__alignof__`) AND the operator forms over them. Before P62 `attrArgAtom` admitted only Identifier / IntLiteral / FloatLiteral / string / nested-parens, and those are KEYWORDS, so no alternative matched and the shipped Xcode SDK's `MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/libkern/OSAtomicDeprecated.h` died at the parser; the first fix admitted the two primaries and left every operator form refused, which three working references contradicted. ★ THE EXIT CODE IS THE ASSERTION. Five keyword-led truth rows SCORE to 42, each placing the decorated member after a `char` so the member OFFSET (and the aggregate's size) moves when the request lands — with the attribute dropped m1 is 16/8 rather than 32/16 and m2/m3 are 2/1 rather than 16/8, so a silent drop cannot score 42. `sizeof(struct pair)` (16) and `_Alignof(struct pair)` (8) are deliberately DIFFERENT, so a row reading the wrong one fails instead of passing by coincidence. Five OPERATOR rows (`2 + 2 * 3`, `sizeof(pair) * 2`, `2 * _Alignof(pair)`, `1 << 4`, `1 ? 8 : 32`) carry NO points and return their OWN exit code instead, so a wrong FOLD is distinguishable from a wrong ROW. `2 + 2 * 3` is the one that matters most: it is 8, and the cheap way to admit operators — a flat left-to-right tail — folds it to 12. A wrong alignment is a wrong LAYOUT that compiles clean, so that row is this file's guard against the silent miscompile. TARGET-INDEPENDENT by construction: `long long` is 8 bytes and 8-aligned on all four targets here, and `long` is deliberately unused (8 under LP64, 4 under LLP64 — it would let the windows arm pass straight through the defect). ✔REFERENCE ORACLE, RUN NOT ASSUMED, each probed SEPARATELY on THIS FILE at -Wall -Wextra: gcc 13.3.0 (WSL) at -std=gnu17 and -std=c2x, clang 18.1.3 (WSL) at -std=gnu17 and -std=c23, and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 all BUILD it with ZERO warnings and EXIT 42. MSVC 19.51 is NOT an oracle for this file and casts no vote on `__attribute__` at all: its CONTROL — the identical construct with an integer-literal operand — is refused by the same C2143, so the refusal isolates to the spelling. Its vote on the real question was taken in its own spelling and it REFUSES there (`__declspec(align(sizeof(int)*2))` and `__declspec(align(2*8))` are error C2059 while `__declspec(align(16))` is rc 0). Three working references to one refusal ⇒ the disjunction requires DSS to accept. ⚠ THE TYPEDEF WITNESS IN THIS FILE CARRIES NO POINTS, DELIBERATELY: a typedef interns to the same TypeId as its aliasee, so a satisfied request (8 on a type already 8-aligned) is a proven no-op with no observable runtime consequence, and the discriminating half of that arm is a REFUSAL which cannot live in a file that must build. It is pinned as AttributeArgConstExpr.TypedefRequestStricterThanTheAliasFailsLoud, whose red proves the operand folded to 16 rather than vanishing; read the two together. RED-ON-DISABLE, three directions: put `attrArgAtom` back as `attrArgItem`'s first element (i.e. take the constant-EXPRESSION level away) and the keyword-led rows still build while every operator row dies at the parser; remove `sizeofExpr`/`alignofExpr` from `attrArgAtom`'s alt and the file does not COMPILE at all (P_NoAlternativeMatched on `sizeof`); remove `attributeArgExprRule` from `semantics.attributeSemantics` and it parses but the operand descent walks past the expression into its type reference and every row fails loud. All three stop it exiting 42.
